help.backend: Where the numbers come from. HWiNFO has the widest coverage (temperatures, fans, voltages). LibreHardwareMonitor is a free alternative. Built-in needs no extra program but has no CPU temperatures or fans. Automatic tries them in that order.
help.bat_rate: Power flowing into (+, charging) or out of (-, discharging) the battery, in watts. While discharging it is roughly what the whole laptop draws.
help.bat_state: On AC: plugged in but not charging. Charging, Discharging or Full otherwise. Comes from Windows, whichever data source is active.
help.bench_cpu: Runs integer and floating-point loops in separate processes: one process for the single-thread score, one per logical core for the multi-thread score. Records the highest temperature, average clock, power and whether the CPU throttled. Detailed mode repeats the runs (median and variation) and keeps all cores busy for 90 s to see whether clock, temperature and speed stay stable.
help.bench_gpu: Starts the small helper GpuBench.exe, which runs a Direct3D 11 compute shader on the fastest graphics card (shader math and video memory bandwidth). Needs no driver add-ons. Records GPU temperature, hot spot, clock and power. Detailed mode runs it three times.
help.bench_mode: Quick measures every test once. Detailed takes about 3 to 4 times longer: it repeats the measurements and shows the average with its variation (± %), adds a sustained-load section (clock and temperature over time), memory block sizes, SSD queue depths and a longer GPU run. History entries remember the mode.
help.bench_ram: Reads, writes and copies large memory blocks with several threads to measure bandwidth, then follows random addresses to estimate access latency (an estimate, not an exact nanosecond figure). Records the DIMM temperatures (SPD hub), memory clock and CPU package power. Detailed mode also measures bandwidth for small and large blocks, which shows the cache levels and where main memory begins.
help.bench_score: Higher is better. The score combines the measurements of a test into one number (geometric mean); the overall score combines the test scores. Scores are comparable only within metriQ - not with other benchmark programs.
help.bench_ssd: Uses a temporary file in your Temp folder (or on the drive picked below), written with caching disabled so the drive itself is measured. Needs at least 4 GB free; the file is deleted afterwards. Records the drive temperature and the peak read / write rate. Detailed mode uses a larger file and also tests several queue depths.
help.bg: Normally closing the panel (X) ends metriQ. Tick a situation here and, while it is active, closing the panel only hides the window: recording and mini mode keep going, and a metriQ icon appears next to the clock. Click it to bring the panel back; right-click it for Exit. Launching metriQ again also shows the hidden panel.
help.columns: How many columns the cards are arranged in. Automatic picks what fits your screen best.
help.decimal: The symbol used for decimals in the CSV (comma or dot). Automatic follows your Windows regional settings, so Excel reads the numbers correctly.
help.delim: The character that separates the columns in the CSV. Automatic follows your Windows regional settings, so Excel opens the file correctly.
help.detail: Also saves a second CSV with one line per program at every sample, so you can see exactly who was busy. It grows quickly.
help.est: A rough guess of the disk space recording uses with the current settings.
help.fan_curve: Sets the fan speed by temperature. Drag the points; double-click empty space to add one, double-click a point to remove it (2-8 points). The red area is below the role's minimum: the fan never goes lower. The vertical line is the current temperature, the dot the current speed.
help.fan_diag: A switch: while on, the fan runs at 100 % with no time limit, so you can look into the case and see which fan it is (on a GPU card, all fans of that GPU). The service accepts only 30 seconds at a time, so metriQ renews it every 10 seconds. It turns off when you press it again, leave this page, close Settings or press STOP.
help.fan_limits: If the CPU or GPU reaches this temperature, all fans go to 100 %.
help.fan_master: While on, metriQ drives the fans with the curves you set. While off, the BIOS controls all fans.
help.fan_profiles: Quick starting points. Each profile sets a temperature curve on all fans except pumps and empty headers.
help.fan_role: The role sets the lowest speed allowed: pump 60 %, CPU / GPU / unknown 30 %, case fan no minimum. An empty header has no fan and always stays under BIOS control.
help.fan_stop: Gives every fan back to the BIOS at once and switches fan control off.
help.filter: Choose which programs go into that second file. By default every program is included.
help.hdr_avg: The average since the panel started, since you last pressed reset (R), or since recording started.
help.hdr_max: The highest value since the panel started, since you last pressed reset (R), or since recording started.
help.hdr_min: The lowest value since the panel started, since you last pressed reset (R), or since recording started.
help.hwpath: Where HWiNFO64.EXE is installed. Automatic usually finds it by itself.
help.interval: How often the panel reads the sensors and writes a line to the CSV, in seconds. Smaller values give finer detail but bigger files.
help.interval_lbl: Seconds between readings and CSV lines. You can also change it in Settings > Logging.
help.keep: CSV files made by the panel that are older than this many days are deleted when it starts. 0 keeps everything.
help.lay_bar: Shows a small bar next to the value for this row.
help.lay_limits: The value shown fully green and the value shown fully red; colours blend in between. Leave both empty for automatic limits. Swap them when low is bad (like FPS).
help.lay_show: Untick to hide a row from the panel. It is then left out of the Panel data CSV too.
help.layout: Choose which rows appear on the panel, and edit their names, order and colour limits. Changes apply with Apply or Save. Reset brings back the automatic layout.
help.lhm: The address of LibreHardwareMonitor's web server. Leave it on auto unless you changed its port.
help.logall: Panel data saves only the rows you see on the panel. All data saves every sensor the data source offers: many more columns and bigger files.
help.logbtn: Click to start or stop recording to a CSV file (or press L). Green means the readings are being saved.
help.logdir: Where the CSV files are saved. Leave it empty to use the default folder.
help.logging: While this is on, the readings are saved to a CSV file you can open in Excel. You can also press L on the panel.
help.lv_nav: Mouse wheel zooms around the pointer, dragging moves the view, a click pins a marker (click it again to remove it) and a double click shows the whole recording. Shift + wheel, the arrow keys and + / - work too.
help.lv_recs: The recording picker lists your recordings, newest first. A red tag means the recording ended abruptly (crash, freeze or power loss), a yellow one means rows are missing in between. Green means it is still being written.
help.lv_series: Tick the series to draw. A group's tick box selects or clears only the series of that group and the arrow only folds the list: neither touches your other picks. The round buttons add a ready-made set of main series (press again to remove just those). Series with the same unit share an axis. The first unit gets the left axis and the second unit the right axis; further units are still drawn (each on its own scale) but have no ruler, so read them from the hover balloon or the statistics table.
help.manage: The panel opens HWiNFO when it starts and closes it when you close the panel. Needs the one-time setup (install.ps1).
help.maxmb: When the CSV reaches this size, the panel starts a new file. 0 means no limit.
help.mini: A small see-through strip with a few readings that stays on top of your game. It works only over games in windowed or borderless (fullscreen windowed) mode: a game in exclusive fullscreen hides it. The strip cannot be clicked, so the mouse and keys always reach the game. metriQ never touches the game itself.
help.mini_bg: Plate puts the readings on a card in the theme colour, which is the easiest to read. Transparent shows only the text, which can be hard to read on bright scenes.
help.mini_hotkey: Shows or hides the strip from anywhere, even inside a game (the strip itself cannot be clicked). On the panel you can also press M. If another program already uses the key combination, metriQ tells you; pick a different one.
help.mini_metrics: Rows of your panel layout (up to 8). The colours follow the same green-to-red limits as on the panel. Leave it as it is to get FPS, CPU / GPU temperature, usage and power where they exist.
help.modebtn: Chooses what is saved: Panel data is only the rows you see on the panel, All data is every sensor. Click to switch.
help.monitor: The screen the panel opens on. Automatic prefers a second, upright (portrait) screen, otherwise your main one.
help.pm: Optional: PresentMon lets the panel show FPS when HWiNFO is not the data source. Leave it empty if you do not need FPS.
help.resetbtn: Starts MIN, MAX and AVG over from now (or press R). Recording is not affected.
help.scan: Checks your recordings for ones that stopped suddenly or have gaps, which can point to a freeze, crash or power loss, and compares them with the Windows event log.
help.stress: Runs a self-checking load until you press Stop. CPU: calculations with known answers (integer, float, SHA-256, CRC); RAM: writes patterns into a few hundred MB and reads them back; GPU: every shader value is computed twice and compared; SSD: numbered blocks are written and read back. A single mismatch counts as an error and stops that test. The run stops by itself above the temperature limit or when the sensors disappear.
help.stress_limit: The test stops automatically when the CPU or GPU temperature goes above this value. Needs a temperature source (HWiNFO gives the most complete data).
help.sync: Sets HWiNFO's own reading speed to your recording interval, so both run in step. Needs the one-time setup (install.ps1).
help.th_auto: Uses 4 equal bands between each row's green and red limits. Untick to set your own thresholds.
help.th_fonts: Pick the typefaces used on the panel. (automatic) lets metriQ choose a good one.
help.th_grad: The five colours that values pass through from good (1) to bad (5), for example green to red as a temperature climbs.
help.th_mode: Smooth fades the colour gradually. Stepped uses a few flat colour bands that change at the thresholds below.
help.th_radius: How round the corners of the cards are.
help.th_spacing: Space between the rows: lower packs more rows in, higher makes the panel airier.
help.th_steps: Where the colour changes, as a percent of each row's green-to-red range. 2 to 4 rising numbers (like 50, 75, 90) give 3 to 5 bands.
help.throttle: Shows why the processor / graphics card is being held back: None, or Thermal (too hot), Power (power limit reached) or PROCHOT (an outside signal such as the laptop's embedded controller slows the CPU). Needs HWiNFO as the data source; with LibreHardwareMonitor or the built-in source there is no throttling information and this row does not appear.
help.top: Adds columns to the CSV with the programs that use the most CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM or disk at each moment. 0 turns a column off.
help.topmost: Keeps the panel above other windows, so it stays visible while you work or play.
help.updates: Looks for a newer metriQ about once a day. Nothing is installed without asking you first.
help.viewbtn: Opens the recording viewer (or press V).
help.window_mode: Maximized fills the screen but keeps the window frame. Full screen hides everything else. Window is a normal window you can move and resize.

strings.applying: setting HWiNFO polling interval to {ms} ms · values held…
strings.cr_d_hot: Unusual values (last value far above the file average):
strings.cr_d_winerr: Windows event log could not be read.
strings.cr_intro: Looks through your recordings for ones that ended abruptly (freeze, power loss, crash) or contain gaps, and matches them with Windows event log entries.
strings.cr_rec_intro: Recordings without problems (clean stop, no gaps). The list refreshes when this tab opens.
strings.cr_select: Select an event to see the details.
strings.cr_sum_abrupt: Recording stopped at {last}, no clean stop
strings.fn_bios_note: The BIOS controls this fan; metriQ leaves it alone.
strings.fn_curve_hint: Drag the points. Double-click empty space to add a point, double-click a point to remove it (2-8 points). The red area is below this role's minimum.
strings.fn_diag_lost: Identify stopped: the fan service did not answer.
strings.fn_enable_err: Fan control could not be changed: the fan service is not reachable.
strings.fn_gpu_all: Mode and curve apply to all fans of this GPU together.
strings.fn_headers_hint: Each card is one fan header; all fans of a GPU share one card. Switch Identify on to find out which fan in the case it is.
strings.fn_limit_hint: At this temperature all fans go to 100 % (CPU 60-95 °C, GPU 60-90 °C).
strings.fn_lost: The fan service is not reachable.
strings.fn_missing: Fan control only works in the installed version (Setup). The portable version has no fan service.
strings.fn_none_note: Empty header: it always stays under BIOS control.
strings.fn_panic: Temperature limit exceeded: all fans at 100 %
strings.fn_pawnio: Motherboard fans need the PawnIO driver (GPU fans work without it).
strings.fn_profiles_hint: Applies a ready-made curve to every fan except pumps and empty headers; pumps run at a fixed 100 %. You can fine-tune each fan afterwards.
strings.fn_risk_1: Every role has a minimum speed: pump at least 60 %, CPU / GPU / unknown fans at least 30 %. The pump and the CPU fan are never lowered below their minimum.
strings.fn_risk_2: If the CPU or GPU temperature limit is exceeded, all fans go to 100 %.
strings.fn_risk_3: If a temperature sensor is lost, the fans that depend on it go to 100 %.
strings.fn_risk_4: Pressing STOP or switching the control off gives the fans back to the BIOS.
strings.fn_risk_intro: Wrong fan settings can overheat the computer and damage hardware. This feature comes without any warranty; you use it at your own risk.
strings.fn_safe: A fan could not return to the BIOS cleanly; the safe curve is used. Restarting the computer gives control back to the BIOS.
strings.fn_save_err: Settings could not be saved: the fan service is not reachable.
strings.fn_starting: The fan service is starting or stopping. Try again in a few seconds.
strings.fn_stop_err: The STOP command did not reach the service! The fans may still be under software control.
strings.fn_stopped: The fan service (metriQFan) is not running. Until it starts, the BIOS controls the fans. You can start it from the Windows Services list and try again.
strings.fn_sub_off: The BIOS is driving the fans
strings.fn_unreach: The fan service does not answer. Wait a moment and try again; if it keeps failing, restart the computer.
strings.fn_unsupported: Fan control is not supported on this device (laptop fans are controlled by the embedded controller). No controllable fan chip was found, so metriQ changes nothing and the fans keep running as the maker designed.
strings.hint_lhm: LibreHardwareMonitor not reachable: start it and enable Options > Remote Web Server > Run (port 8085)
strings.hint_no_shm: HWiNFO is running but shared memory is off: Settings > Shared Memory Support
strings.hint_not_running: HWiNFO is not running: start HWiNFO64 in sensors mode
strings.hint_readonly: read-only mode (run install.ps1 to let the panel start/stop HWiNFO)
strings.log_err: recording failed: the CSV file cannot be written
strings.lv_hint: Wheel: zoom   Drag: pan   Click: pin   Double click: reset
strings.lv_nosel: Pick a quick group or tick series on the left.
strings.lv_prog_none: No program data at this moment.
strings.lv_stats_tip: Show or hide the table of min / avg / max values
strings.lv_tip_all: Draws every series of the groups you already have series from and shows the whole range. Press again to remove just those.
strings.lv_tip_check: Select / unselect every series of this group. Other groups are not touched.
strings.lv_tip_open: Only opens or closes the list. Your selection stays as it is.
strings.lv_tip_preset: Adds this group's main series. Press again to remove exactly those.
strings.lv_tip_prog: Show or hide the programs running at the cursor
strings.mini_enable: Show mini mode when metriQ starts
strings.mini_hk_taken: Mini mode hotkey {combo} is used by another program: choose another in Settings > Mini mode
strings.mini_metrics_hint: Tick up to {n} rows of your layout; they appear in this order.
strings.mini_no_rows: No rows yet: waiting for sensor data.
strings.na_adl: AMD GPU temperature, clock, power and fan are not available: ADL ({err}).
strings.na_driver: CPU / motherboard temperatures, fans, voltages and CPU power need a signed kernel driver: choose HWiNFO or LibreHardwareMonitor as data source.
strings.na_fps: FPS: optional, needs PresentMon (Settings > Data source).
strings.na_gpu_other: GPU: load and VRAM only (temperature, clock and power need an NVIDIA GPU (NVML), an AMD GPU (ADL), HWiNFO or LibreHardwareMonitor).
strings.na_nvml: NVIDIA GPU temperature, clock, power and fan are not available: NVML ({err}).
strings.na_pdh: Windows performance counters unavailable ({err}): no core, network or disk data. Install psutil (pip install psutil) or repair the counters (lodctr /r as admin).
strings.na_pdh_psutil: Windows performance counters unavailable ({err}): using psutil (no core clocks).
strings.na_pm_err: FPS: PresentMon error: {err} (it needs admin rights or the 'Performance Log Users' group).
strings.pf_close_q: A benchmark is running. Stop it and close?
strings.pf_confirm:
{tests} ({mode}) will put your PC under full load for about {secs}. Fans will get loud, temperatures rise. On a laptop, plug in the charger.

Start now?
strings.pf_cpu_d: Integer and floating-point kernels, first on one thread, then on all threads. Detailed adds repeated runs (median) and a 90 s sustained-load section.
strings.pf_cpupower: CPU package power avg {v:.0f} W / max {m:.0f} W
strings.pf_curve: Read bandwidth by block size (cache to main memory)
strings.pf_curve_sum: Fastest: {fast:.0f} GB/s at {fsz}, main memory: {slow:.0f} GB/s at {ssz}
strings.pf_gpu_d: Direct3D 11 compute shader in two phases: shader math (draws up to the power limit), then video memory bandwidth (the shader cores mostly wait, so less power). Each phase warms up first; only the settled part is scored. Detailed runs three times in a row and shows how clock and temperature hold up.
strings.pf_hist_hint: Select a row to show that run in the cards above.
strings.pf_intro: Measures what this PC can do: CPU, memory, SSD and graphics card, together with temperatures, clocks and power during the run. Scores are comparable only within metriQ - they do not replace other benchmarks.
strings.pf_mode_hint_detailed: Detailed: about 3x longer - every test is repeated (mean and variation), plus a sustained-load section, memory block sizes, SSD queue depths and a longer GPU run. About {t} for all four tests.
strings.pf_mode_hint_quick: Quick: one pass of every test, about {t} for all four tests.
strings.pf_overall_none: Run the tests to get a score
strings.pf_ram_d: Read, write and copy bandwidth with large buffers plus random-access latency. Detailed adds repeated runs and a bandwidth curve over block sizes (cache to DRAM).
strings.pf_ssd_d: Sequential 1 MB read/write with 8 requests in flight and random 4K read/write on a temporary file, cache bypassed. Detailed uses a larger file, repeated runs and more queue depths.
strings.pf_ssd_free: Free space on {drive}: {gb:.0f} GB. The test writes a {size:g} GB temporary file (deleted afterwards).
strings.pf_ssd_hdd: This drive is a hard disk (HDD) or behind a slow bus: about 100-250 MB/s is normal there.
strings.pf_ssd_low: Only {gb:.1f} GB free on {drive}: the SSD test will be skipped (needs {need} GB).
strings.pf_sus_sum: Clock {cmin:.0f}-{cmax:.0f} MHz ({cd:+.1f} % first to last fifth), temperature {t0}{t1}, max {tm}{perf}. {thr}
strings.pf_warn: The test puts the PC under full load: fans get loud and the CPU / GPU get hot. Close other programs. On a laptop, plug in the charger first.
strings.pl_big: The CSV file is over 1 GB: consider a size limit in Settings > Logging
strings.pl_side_err: recording failed: the process CSV file cannot be written
strings.ps_bad_limit: The temperature limits must be between {lo} and {hi} °C.
strings.ps_chart_cap: Clock and temperature over time (each line has its own scale)
strings.ps_confirm:
The {what} test will put your PC under full load until you press Stop. Fans will get loud and temperatures rise (automatic stop: CPU {cpu} °C, GPU {gpu} °C). Save your work and close other programs. On a laptop, plug in the charger.

Start now?
strings.ps_desc: Keeps the chosen parts under full load until you press Stop and checks every result: wrong calculations, memory or disk data errors and GPU errors mean the part is unstable. It also stops by itself when a temperature limit is exceeded.
strings.ps_detail_hint: one row per program and sample
strings.ps_err_banner: ERROR in the {part} test: {msg}. That test was stopped - this part is not stable (at these settings).
strings.ps_keep_hint: 0 = keep all; older files are deleted at start
strings.ps_maxmb_hint: 0 = no limit; a new file is started above it
strings.ps_note_notemp: No temperature sensor is available (install HWiNFO for temperatures): the automatic temperature stop is inactive - watch the temperatures yourself.
strings.ps_stop_failed: Stopped: every selected test failed (see the errors).
strings.ps_stop_sensors: Stopped automatically: the temperature sensors stopped responding (is HWiNFO still running?).
strings.ps_sum_ssd: SSD: drive {tmax}; read peak {rp}, write peak {wp}
strings.ps_top_hint: 0 = off; 1–99 = number of programs added as columns
strings.pw_all_tip: On: every program goes into the process CSV. Off: only the ones you switch on below.
strings.pw_kernel_tip:
Memory in use that belongs to no program: kernel and driver memory (paged / non-paged pool), page tables, modified file cache and memory shared between programs.
= RAM in use (total - available, like the panel) - the programs' private working sets.
strings.pw_locked_tip: Every program is logged. Turn off "Log all programs" to choose.
strings.pw_other_tip: {n} programs below the limits above, added up. Set a limit to 0 to list them one by one.
strings.pw_pill_tip: Add this program to the process CSV
strings.pw_show_all_tip: Ignores the limits and lists every running program.
strings.pw_sum_ram: RAM in use {used} = programs {prog} + Windows kernel & drivers {kern}
strings.sr_intro: Saves a text file with every sensor the current data source reports and which panel rows found a value. It contains no user name, computer name, folder paths or serial numbers. Handy when something is missing on your hardware: send us the file.
strings.st_bg_keep: When the panel is closed, keep running in the background
strings.st_hw_only: HWiNFO only: these options are used only while HWiNFO is the active data source.
strings.st_invalid: Check the fields marked in red.
strings.st_lay_auto_note: Automatic layout (editing anything turns it into your own layout).
strings.st_lay_empty: No layout yet: waiting for sensor data.
strings.st_lay_reset_q: Go back to the automatic layout? The custom layout is removed from config.json when you save.
strings.st_lhm_hint: auto = http://127.0.0.1:8085/data.json · in LibreHardwareMonitor: Options > Remote Web Server > Run
strings.st_manage: Start HWiNFO with the panel and stop it when the panel closes
strings.st_missing: Not available with the active source
strings.st_pm_hint: optional, experimental: PresentMon console exe, FPS for LHM / built-in · empty = off
strings.st_sync: Set HWiNFO's polling interval to the logging interval
strings.st_tasks_no: Scheduled tasks: not installed. Run install.ps1 (see README) so the panel can start / stop HWiNFO and set its interval; until then these two options have no effect.
strings.st_tasks_ok: Scheduled tasks: installed (the panel can start / stop HWiNFO without a UAC prompt).
strings.th_auto: Automatic: 4 equal bands from each row's limits
strings.th_colors_hint: Click a swatch to change it, right-click to reset it.
strings.th_pick_hint: Picking a theme clears your customisations.
strings.th_steps_hint: % of each row's range: 2-4 ascending values (e.g. 50, 75, 90) = 3-5 bands.
strings.tray_balloon: The panel was closed, but metriQ keeps running in the background. Click the tray icon to show the panel again; right-click it for more options.
strings.upd_confirm:
metriQ v{v} is available (this is v{cur}).

Download and install it now? The panel closes and starts again after the update.
strings.upd_confirm_src:
metriQ v{v} is available (this is v{cur}).

Open the download page?
strings.why_hw_manage_off: Built-in source: HWiNFO is not running (starting HWiNFO with the panel is switched off). Start HWiNFO64 or switch the option on.
strings.why_hw_none: Built-in source: temperatures and power need HWiNFO, and HWiNFO64 is not installed. Install it from hwinfo.com, then run the metriQ Setup again.
strings.why_hw_noshm: Built-in source: HWiNFO is running but its shared memory is off. In HWiNFO: Settings > Shared Memory Support (the free version switches it off after 12 hours: restart HWiNFO).
strings.why_hw_notasks: Built-in source: HWiNFO is installed but not running, and the panel cannot start it (its scheduled tasks are missing). Run the metriQ Setup again, or start HWiNFO64 yourself.
